name: Atlas
tagline: Copperplate engraving — indigo ink on laid paper
technique: Copperplate engraving as in the Encyclopédie (1751–72) and natural-history plates: burin lines and cross-hatching for tone, one exploded or cutaway object per plate, indigo ink on cream laid paper.
avoid: decks read mostly on phones (hatching dies at small sizes)

plates.accept: Exploded object in true hatching, indigo on cream; left third empty; no text or numbers.
Botanical subject in true engraving; no text or numbers.
Mechanical cutaway in true engraving; no text or numbers.
A single symmetric horizontal ornament; nothing else.
Ink-only engraving of an eye on pure white; no text.
Ink-only engraving of a hand with quill on pure white; no text.
Ink-only engraving of a key on pure white; no text.

generate.base: A copperplate engraving of {subject}, printed in indigo ink on cream laid paper: fine burin lines, cross-hatching and stipple for tone, one exploded or cutaway object as in an 18th-century encyclopedia plate. No cartouche, no numbers, no labels, no faces.
generate.spot: A single copperplate engraving of {subject}, printed in indigo ink: fine burin lines, cross-hatching and stipple for tone, crisp 18th-century style, ink lines only.
generate.rules: No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature anywhere in the image.

prompts.hero.webp: A copperplate engraving printed in indigo ink on cream laid paper: an antique brass letter balance (postal scale) shown as an exploded diagram — the beam, the two pans, the chains, the pillar and the weights floating apart from each other in an orderly way — rendered with fine burin lines, cross-hatching and stipple for tone, crisp and precise like an 18th-century encyclopedia plate. The object fills the right two thirds; the left third of the paper is empty. Visible laid-paper chain lines. No cartouche, no numbers, no labels, no faces. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature anywhere in the image.
